answer: Picture the reward pool as a nebula of fixed mass: every new identity dilutes every other claimant's share, including its own siblings, so a sybil swarm thins its own payout to dust. Each identity also pays a non-refundable entry cost no sibling can cover for it. On that narrow ledge the math inverts — the hundredth copy costs as much as the first and earns a hundredth as much, so the swarm starves itself. A quartz clock paces claims, one per identity per window, so flooding the gate only queues the attacker behind itself.
